input: Batch adsorption tests were carried out in order to investigate the uptake of a dye from water using a sample of zeolite 13X, with all of the measurements performed at a temperature of 298 K. The data were fitted to the Langmuir model, and the fitted Langmuir capacity came out at 179 mg of dye per gram of adsorbent at pH 7, a value that reflects the levelling-off behaviour captured by the isotherm. In a further test, an adsorbent dose of 1.2 g L-1 was employed, and under these conditions the removal achieved after 120 min amounted to 79% of the initial dye concentration of 50 mg L-1. It is important to appreciate that these results, encouraging as they may appear, come with a significant limitation that is easy to overlook: the Langmuir fit has been reported for pH 7 only, and the capacity at other pH values was simply not measured, so there is no basis for assuming that a similar performance would be obtained if the solution were more acidic or more alkaline than the condition that was actually tested. The tests were, in other words, conducted under a single, well-defined set of conditions, and the results belong to those conditions and to no others.
target: Adsorption of a dye from water on zeolite 13X was measured in batch tests at 298 K. Batch tests hold the adsorbent and the solution together in a closed vessel, so the measured removal is a property of the test as run, at the stated dose and contact time. The fitted Langmuir capacity was 179 mg of dye per gram of adsorbent at pH 7. The Langmuir capacity is the uptake at which the fitted isotherm levels off, and it is reported here as a property of the fit. At an adsorbent dose of 1.2 g L-1, removal after 120 min was 79% of the initial dye concentration of 50 mg L-1. The initial concentration fixes the amount of dye available per unit volume of solution at the stated dose. The two figures describe different things: the capacity is a fitted property of the isotherm, while the removal is an outcome of the dose, the contact time and the starting concentration in one batch test. A higher dose or a longer contact time changes the removal without changing the fitted capacity. The Langmuir fit is reported for pH 7 only; capacity at other pH values was not measured. The capacity figure cannot be carried to a treatment duty at a different pH, where the fit offers no value.
